subtitle: From Regent’s Shadow to City of Copper and Stone

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye wide of a half-built ancient city near a lake, with Pravarasena II in the foreground overlooking plans and copperplates
panels.action: Pravarasena II stands on a rocky rise, scrolls and copperplates at his feet, watching masons raise temples and halls in a sprawling new cityscape by the waters of a Vidarbha lake.

dialogue.text: In the shadow of a Gupta princess, a Vakataka prince renamed himself Pravarasena and raised a new capital, Pravarapura—writing his freedom into copper and stone.

i18n.hi: गुप्त राजकुमारी की छाया में पला वाकाटक युवराज अपना नाम बदलकर प्रवरसेन बना और नई राजधानी प्रवरपुर उठाई — अपनी आज़ादी तांबे और शिला पर लिख दी।

panels.shot: moody interior medium shot in a palace hall, low-angle on a young prince beside a veiled royal figure seated on a throne
panels.action: A younger Damodarasena stands at the side of a high-backed throne, hands folded, while an older queenly silhouette, recalling Prabhavatigupta, presides over courtiers beneath painted wooden beams.

dialogue.text: Before he was Pravarasena, he was Damodarasena, son of the Gupta princess Prabhavatigupta, growing to manhood under her regency in Nandivardhana’s guarded halls.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन बनने से पहले वह दामोदरसेन था — गुप्त राजकुमारी प्रभावतीगुप्ता का बेटा — जो नंदिवर्धन के कड़े पहरे वाले महलों में उसकी रीजेंसी के सहारे जवान हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Pravarasena II’s face in profile as he listens to a court Brahmin recite a copperplate grant
panels.action: In a lamplit chamber, Damodarasena watches an elder Brahmin trace lines on a copperplate, his own face half in shadow, half in the warm glow of the lamp.

dialogue.text: In those years the queen ruled in her father Chandragupta II’s name, but the boy listened, learning how power flowed through land grants and the measured words of Brahmins.

i18n.hi: उन वर्षों में रानी अपने पिता चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय के नाम से राज चलाती रही, और वह बालक सुनता रहा, सीखता रहा कि सत्ता कैसे भूमि दान और ब्राह्मणों की नाप‑तौल भरी वाणी से बहती है।

panels.shot: transition wide shot of a funeral pyre in the distance with the palace silhouetted, then focus on the prince standing apart
panels.action: Smoke rises from a royal cremation ground beyond the palace; Damodarasena stands apart on a terrace, the wind tugging his cloak as courtiers whisper behind him.

dialogue.text: In time, Prabhavatigupta’s long regency ended. The Gupta shadow thinned, and the son faced a question that no copperplate could answer for him.

i18n.hi: समय आया, प्रभावतीगुप्ता की लंबी रीजेंसी खत्म हुई। गुप्तों की छाया हल्की पड़ी, और बेटे के सामने सवाल खड़ा हुआ, जिसका जवाब कोई ताम्रपत्र नहीं दे सकता था।

panels.shot: medium close-up, frontal, Damodarasena in a private shrine placing a garland on a linga, expression steady
panels.action: Inside a small stone shrine, Damodarasena lays a fresh garland on a Shiva linga, his hand steady, a single shaft of light falling on his face as he looks up in resolve.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: I must be more than my mother’s son.

i18n.hi: मुझे सिर्फ अपनी माँ का बेटा नहीं रहना।

panels.shot: ceremonial wide shot in a court hall, low-angle on the prince being anointed while a herald holds up a copperplate with new titulature
panels.action: In the crowded audience hall, priests anoint Damodarasena with sacred water as a herald lifts a gleaming copperplate, courtiers bowing while the prince’s new name is formally proclaimed.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions no longer called him Damodarasena. They named him Pravarasena, evoking the dynasty’s great ancestor, signalling that a new, self-confident king now spoke for Vakataka power.

i18n.hi: लेखों में अब उसका नाम दामोदरसेन नहीं रहा। वे उसे प्रवरसेन कहने लगे, वंश के महापुरुख की याद दिलाते हुए — संकेत कि अब आत्मविश्वासी नया राजा वाकाटक शक्ति की आवाज़ बन चुका है।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind Pravarasena looking down at a spread of land-grant copperplates on a low table
panels.action: Seated cross-legged, Pravarasena studies several copperplates laid out before him, each inscribed with neat lines, as attendants wait with styluses and blank sheets.

dialogue.text: His reign speaks to us through copper and script. The Chammak, Thalner and Balaghat charters show a king who governed by grant and record, not by boastful battle lists.

i18n.hi: उसका राज हमसे तांबे और लेखन के ज़रिए बोलता है; चमक, थालनेर और बालाघाट के ताम्रपत्र बताते हैं कि यह राजा दान और दस्तावेज़ से राज करता था, न कि शेखी भरी विजय सूचियों से।

panels.shot: map-like high-angle shot over a desk where Pravarasena traces routes on a palm-leaf map of Vidarbha and beyond
panels.action: With a reed stylus, Pravarasena traces river lines on a palm-leaf map, small markers showing places like Chammak and Thalner, while a councillor points toward the north-western frontier.

dialogue.text: The plates mark his movements—Chammak on the Wardha, Thalner by the Tapti, Balaghat in the interior. They hint at a ruler touring his lands, anchoring them with gifts and charters.

i18n.hi: ये पट्ट उसके कदमों के निशान भी खींचते हैं — वर्धा किनारे चमक, तापती तट पर थालनेर, भीतरी भूभाग में बालाघाट — मानो कोई राजा देश‑देश घूमकर दान और सनदों से अपनी धरती जकड़ रहा हो।

panels.shot: wide landscape shot of the Mansar-Ramtek hills and lake, with Pravarasena on horseback in the foreground surveying the site
panels.action: On a ridge above a calm lake and rolling hills, Pravarasena sits astride a horse, flanked by surveyors with measuring cords, pointing toward the slopes where future buildings will stand.

dialogue.text: North-east of Nandivardhana, by the hills of today’s Ramtek and the waters near Mansar, he saw a new capital in the land itself—though our knowledge of its exact outlines comes from later excavation.

i18n.hi: नंदिवर्धन के उत्तर‑पूर्व, आज के रामटेक की पहाड़ियों और मानसार के जल के पास, उसने धरती में ही एक नई राजधानी देखी — भले ही उसके सही रूप को हम बाद की खुदाइयों से ही टटोल पाते हैं।

panels.shot: dynamic construction-site wide shot, slightly low-angle, with scaffolds, stone blocks, and a central Shiva temple complex rising
panels.action: Masons haul stone blocks up wooden ramps, carpenters fit beams, and in the center a sanctum’s walls rise, while Pravarasena stands amidst chalked ground-plans giving a quiet instruction.

dialogue.text: Archaeology at Mansar reveals a planned complex—palace, halls, a great Shaiva shrine scholars call Pravareshvara—traces that match the capital Pravarapura named in his charters.

i18n.hi: मानसार की खुदाई एक योजनाबद्ध परिसर दिखाती है — महल, सभा‑भवन, और एक महान शैव मंदिर जिसे विद्वान ‘प्रवरेश्वर’ कहते हैं — ऐसे निशान जो उसके ताम्रपत्रों में वर्णित राजधानी प्रवरपुर से मेल खाते हैं।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot inside a partially built Pravareshvara shrine, with Pravarasena touching a pillar carved with early motifs
panels.action: Within the dim shell of the rising temple, Pravarasena runs his fingers along the rough surface of a newly erected pillar, its base already bearing carved lotus motifs.

dialogue.text: Here, a Shaiva king could root his name in sacred stone. The very temple, Pravareshvara, carried his royal epithet, binding devotion, dynasty and city together.

i18n.hi: यहीं एक शैव राजा अपना नाम पवित्र शिला में रोप सकता था; स्वयं मंदिर प्रवरेश्वर ने उसके राजोपाधि को धारण किया, भक्ति, वंश और नगर — तीनों को एक सूत्र में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a ceremonial procession entering Pravarapura, with gateway structures and the city’s first buildings around
panels.action: Under a temporary wooden gateway, Pravarasena rides into the nascent city, banners fluttering, Brahmins and officials following on foot as townsfolk watch from newly built platforms and courtyards.

dialogue.text: When his grants begin to mention Pravarapura, it is more than a name. It is a statement: the Vakatakas would not only inherit, they would found and name in their own right.

i18n.hi: जब उसके दानपत्रों में प्रवरपुर का नाम उभरता है, वह सिर्फ नाम नहीं; वह घोषणा है — वाकाटक सिर्फ उत्तराधिकार नहीं लेंगे, वे अपने दम पर बसाएँगे, नाम देंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a court at Pravarapura, Pravarasena listening as a scribe reads out a land grant to assembled Brahmins
panels.action: Seated on a low throne in a pillared hall, Pravarasena listens as a court scribe reads from a fresh copperplate while a group of Brahmins sit before him, hands raised in blessing.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: Let this land sustain their learning, and let the record outlast us all.

i18n.hi: यह भूमि उनकी विद्या को पोसे, और यह लेख हम सब से लंबे समय तक साँस लेते रहें।

panels.shot: close-up of a craftsman’s hands incising letters on a glowing strip of copper, Pravarasena’s silhouette faintly reflected
panels.action: A royal engraver leans over a strip of polished copper, carefully incising lines of Brahmi script, while the faint reflection of Pravarasena’s figure shimmers on the metal surface.

dialogue.text: Those plates record more than piety. They show a functioning administration—boundaries fixed, taxes remitted, rights and exemptions spelled out in precise, formulaic words.

i18n.hi: वे पट्ट केवल भक्ति नहीं, पूरा तंत्र लिखते हैं — सीमाएँ तय, कर माफ़, अधिकार और छूटें कठोर, सूत्रबद्ध शब्दों में साफ़‑साफ़ दर्ज।

panels.shot: contrasting wide shot of a peaceful Pravarapura street with traders and monks, hinting at stability
panels.action: A quiet street in Pravarapura shows merchants arranging wares, a group of monks walking by, and children chasing one another across a sunlit courtyard between brick houses.

dialogue.text: The absence of war-boasts in his records does not prove a world without conflict, but it does suggest a reign remembered for order and patronage more than for conquest.

i18n.hi: उसके लेखों में युद्ध‑शेखी की कमी यह नहीं कहती कि जग में झगड़ा न था, पर यह ज़रूर बताती है कि उसका राज ज़्यादा व्यवस्था और दान‑पोषण के लिए याद रहा, विजय जुलूसों के लिए कम।

panels.shot: evening-time medium shot of Pravarasena on a balcony overlooking Pravarapura, the Pravareshvara complex visible in the distance
panels.action: At dusk, Pravarasena leans on a stone parapet, gazing over the rooftops and the silhouetted Pravareshvara complex, the sky behind them washed in orange and purple.

dialogue.speaker: pravarasena_ii
dialogue.text: One day, they will know I was here—not only by whose daughter I was born.

i18n.hi: एक दिन वे जानेंगे कि मैं यहाँ था — सिर्फ इसलिए नहीं कि मैं किसकी बेटी से जन्मा था।

panels.shot: modern-era bird’s-eye shot of the excavated foundations at Mansar and Ramtek hills beyond, with ghostly overlay of imagined ancient Pravarapura
panels.action: From high above, the stone foundations at Mansar sit like scars in the earth, the Ramtek hills rising beyond, while faint, almost transparent forms of halls and temples suggest the ancient city that once stood here.

dialogue.text: Today archaeologists carefully match these foundations with his charters, piecing together Pravarapura’s plan and testing, line by line, how far our reconstructions can safely go.

i18n.hi: आज पुरातत्ववेत्ता इन नींवों को उसके ताम्रपत्रों से जोड़कर देखते हैं, टुकड़ा‑टुकड़ा कर के प्रवरपुर की रूपरेखा गढ़ते हैं, और हर पंक्ति पर परखते हैं कि हमारी कल्पना कहाँ तक सुरक्षित जा सकती है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on an excavated inscription fragment and a Pravarasena copperplate laid side by side on a scholar’s table
panels.action: On a wooden table, a corroded inscription fragment from Mansar lies beside a well-preserved copperplate of Pravarasena, a scholar’s hand pointing to matching names and titles on both.

dialogue.text: Hans Bakker and other scholars read these traces cautiously, connecting the Pravareshvara complex and the capital named Pravarapura—but always with the humility that some stones still keep their secrets.

i18n.hi: हंस बक्कर और दूसरे विद्वान इन निशानों को सँभल‑सँभलकर पढ़ते हैं, प्रवरेश्वर परिसर को प्रवरपुर नामक राजधानी से जोड़ते हुए — पर हमेशा यह मानकर कि कुछ पत्थर अब भी अपनी बातें छिपाए बैठे हैं।

panels.shot: final reflective shot, medium close-up of Pravarasena’s calm, weathered face fading into the outline of Pravarapura’s ruins
panels.action: Pravarasena’s composed face fills the frame, then subtly blends into the worn outlines of ruins on a hillside, the sense of his presence lingering over the broken stones.

dialogue.text: Pravarasena II did not carve fame with spectacular wars; he proved his independence by founding a city, a temple and a paper trail—reminding us that lasting power is often written quietly, in capitals and charters.

i18n.hi: प्रवरसेन द्वितीय ने अपना नाम बड़े युद्धों से नहीं, एक नगर, एक मंदिर और दस्तावेज़ों की कड़ी से गढ़ा — reminding us कि टिकाऊ शक्ति अक्सर चुपचाप, राजधानियों और ताम्रपत्रों में लिखी जाती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: From Regent’s Shadow to City of Copper and Stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: राजमाता की छाया से तांबे‑पत्थर के नगर तक
